problems.description: 41 naming violations (Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase, Constants should be UPPER_CASE) in generator.test.ts, incremental.test.ts, and server.test.ts drive the convention score to 0.57.
Cognitive complexity +14 per SonarQube, driven by large test functions stacking many assertions.
Pervasive non-null assertions (page!.) in tests bypass potentially missing return values instead of asserting on them.

strengths: Comprehensive coverage of parseMarkdownFile, readContentDirectory, and generateSite, including edge cases (empty/nonexistent dirs, empty frontmatter, code blocks, missing tags).
Clean temp-dir lifecycle with beforeEach cleanup and afterAll teardown.
Zero bugs, zero smells, and zero duplication per SonarQube; no new imports or functions outside the test surface.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid greenfield session-1 test suite with strong coverage and clean lifecycle management, rated down only by strict naming-convention flags that look like style-rule noise in test files rather than genuine architecture problems (convention score 0.57 reflects the linter, not structural debt).

problems.description: 41 convention violations (score 0.57) — 'Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase' and 'Constants should be UPPER_CASE' flagged across generator.test.ts, incremental.test.ts, and server.test.ts; per the measurements these are treated as ground truth.
Each of the 9 TemplateEngine tests hand-repeats the same mkdirSync/writeFile scaffolding instead of sharing a setup helper, so the suite is verbose and any layout-path change touches every test.

A ~360-line block (helper + two new describe suites) was appended after the closing brace of the first describe, and createTemplatesDir was defined after its consumers rather than with the other helpers at the top of the file.
Cognitive complexity +9 per SonarQube, driven by the layered render/fallback cases in the new suites; assert-helper dedup would reduce it.

strengths: Reuses existing test conventions — tmpDir, createContentDir, writeFile — so the new suites are consistent with the surrounding file
Thorough coverage of TemplateEngine edge cases: partials, custom layout, custom template, fallback-to-content, and missing-templates-dir null path
New frontmatter test asserts layout/template extraction end-to-end through parseMarkdownFile, tying the feature to the generator contract
commit_reviews.summary: Solid, pattern-following test coverage for the template engine feature, but the 0.57 convention score and ~360 lines of hand-duplicated test scaffolding add real maintainability debt to the test suite.

problems.description: Mechanical measurement attributes PascalCase/UPPER_CASE naming violations to server.test.ts, pulling the convention score to 0.57. The visible diff shows functions and consts only, so this is likely noise from SonarQube's TS analysis or pre-existing violations carried in from generator.test.ts/incremental.test.ts (sessions 1-2), not a clear defect in this commit's new code.

@types/ws (a types-only package) was added to runtime 'dependencies' rather than 'devDependencies'; the lockfile also silently drops 'dev: true' from @types/node as a transitive side effect, broadening the production dependency surface.
chokidar and ws are declared as runtime deps for what appears to be a development live-reload server; if the watcher/WebSocket path is dev-only they belong in devDependencies.

Tests cover the HTTP injection and file-serving paths (200/404/root index) but not the live-reload WebSocket broadcast or file-change trigger that the new deps actually enable, so the integration surface is partially untested.

strengths: Integration tests bind to an ephemeral port (port: 0) and clean up temp dirs and servers in afterEach/afterAll, avoiding port conflicts and leftover state.
Good edge-case coverage of injectLiveReload (no closing body tag, multiple body tags) plus real-request behavior (200, 404, root->index.html).
Dependency wiring matches the live-reload feature intent (chokidar for file watching, ws for push), consistent with the story's incremental session architecture.
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound session-3 integration commit with clean HTTP-level tests and correctly scoped live-reload deps, but the 0.57 convention score comes mostly from naming-rule noise in test files, and @types/ws should live in devDependencies.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +41 from per-plugin optional-method checks nested in the page loop; a single dispatch table or registry would keep the generator flat.
Lifecycle hook asymmetry: the empty-content early return calls onEnd but skips afterBuild, while the normal path calls afterBuild then onEnd — hook ordering is inconsistent between code paths.
loadPluginsFromConfig uses dynamic require() on a computed path and silently swallows all errors, defeating static analysis, breaking under ESM, and hiding misconfigurations.
Convention score 0.57 with 41 violations: test files (generator.test.ts, incremental.test.ts, server.test.ts) declare classes/interfaces in lowerCamelCase and constants not in UPPER_CASE.
New plugin modules (plugin.ts, plugins/markdown, plugins/template, plugins/devserver) are untested; only the server.test.ts tmp-dir path changed.

strengths: Extracts a coherent plugin system, moving markdown parsing and templating out of the monolithic generator
Preserves the public API surface via re-exported parseMarkdownFile and readContentDirectory
Zero new bugs, -1 smell, no duplications per SonarQube
DevServer decoupled into plugins/, keeping live-reload out of core generation
commit_reviews.summary: A genuinely better modular refactor (plugin extraction with backward-compatible exports and zero new bugs), but it lands on a 0.57 convention score and carries real debt via an inconsistent plugin lifecycle and a dynamic require() that swallows errors.

problems.description: 41 naming violations (Classes/Interfaces should be PascalCase, Constants UPPER_CASE) flagged across incremental.test.ts, generator.test.ts, server.test.ts; convention score 0.57

Discrepancy: convention violations reference generator.test.ts and server.test.ts which are not in this commit's +2-file AST diff, so the 0.57 score partly reflects whole-worktree state, not purely this commit
475-line test file repeats identical helper functions (writeFile, createContentDir, createTemplatesDir) instead of sharing a fixture module
SonarQube delta +4 smells and +3 cognitive complexity in the new cache/manifest logic
Build cache manifest persisted inside contentDir (.ssg-cache.json) mixes cache state with source content, risking accidental commits
Skip assertions rely on setting mtime to epoch and expecting it to remain 0; deterministic here but couples test to filesystem timestamp semantics

strengths: Coherent cross-cutting feature: incremental build cache with content hashing and template-directory hash invalidation
Thorough coverage of edge cases: corrupted manifest, template change detection, first-build bootstrap, always-rebuilt index
Clean public API surface (BuildCache load/updateManifest/finalize/persist/clear + shouldSkipFile) exercised end to end via generateSite options object
Index-always-rebuilt behavior explicitly pinned by a test, protecting a subtle correctness invariant
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured incremental-build cache feature backed by solid test coverage, dragged to neutral by naming-convention violations and a bloated duplicated-helper test file.

compounding_issues: Mismatched seed: the initial codebase was an Express Todo API, unrelated to static site generation, forcing Session 1's greenfield build to discard it entirely with zero reuse
node_modules (5,205 files) and dist/ committed to git with no .gitignore — every commit bloated; repo hygiene issue persists to session 5
Flat content scanning (only top-level .md files) carried from Session 1 through Session 5 — nested content directories are silently ignored

Incremental-cache template-hash ordering bug in Session 5 (updateManifest wrote the template hash per-page, causing premature skips) needed a finalize() rework, indicating subtle state-ordering risk in the new cache layer
BuildStats.timeSaved is hardcoded to '0ms', a placeholder stat that misrepresents the cache's actual benefit
key_decisions: Full greenfield rebuild in Session 1 (markdown parser + page/index renderer + CLI), abandoning the unrelated Todo-API seed
Externalizing rendering into a Handlebars template engine with layouts/partials in Session 2 rather than extending inline string templates
Adding a dev server with chokidar file watching and WebSocket live-reload in Session 3
Extracting a plugin architecture in Session 4 (MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin/DevServerPlugin + ssg.config.ts), shrinking generator.ts from 122 to 29 lines while keeping all 35 tests green
Introducing an incremental build cache (MD5 content hashing + .ssg-cache.json manifest) in Session 5 as the cross-cutting optimization layer
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically across all five sessions. Test coverage grew every session (14 -> 28 -> 35 -> 35 -> 56 tests) with all suites passing at each commit, and the architecture matured from a single 122-line generator module into a clean plugin system with separate markdown, template, and dev-server concerns. Session 4's refactor was behavioral-preserving (test count unchanged, tests green) and set up Session 5's cache cleanly. Session 5 added real complexity — a persistent manifest, content and template hashing, skip logic — and the agent actively debugged subtle template-hash ordering issues, ending in a solid, fully-tested state. The only plateau was Session 3, which added the dev server without refactoring, and even that maintained green tests. Overall the arc reads as: solid foundation -> feature layering -> integration -> structural consolidation -> cross-cutting optimization, with no functional regressions along the way.
story_review.summary: A well-executed, highly coherent five-session progression from greenfield SSG core to templated, dev-server-integrated, plugin-architected, incrementally-cached static site generator, with tests growing and staying green at every step.
